epic_title: Importing existing configuration and coexisting with other plugins
summary: This epic gets an existing user's configuration into Calendaric's own shape: reading it out of the core Daily Notes plugin, the Calendar plugin and the Periodic Notes plugin, offering it as a reviewable, reversible import rather than a silent overwrite, and turning off the plugins it replaces only with consent. It also covers noticing when one of those plugins is still active so Calendaric does not fight it, and keeping Calendaric's own stored configuration loadable across its own version changes. It stops short of defining the target configuration shape (SET) and recognising notes already on disk (NOTE/FMT).

stories.title: Import configuration from the core Daily Notes plugin
stories.story: As someone who already uses Obsidian's built-in Daily Notes plugin, I want Calendaric to offer to copy its folder, format and template into my day configuration, so that I do not have to retype settings I already have working.
stories.rationale: This vault currently has the core Daily Notes plugin configured and enabled, so this is a real, present-day migration path, not a hypothetical one.

acceptance_criteria.given: the core Daily Notes plugin is enabled and Calendaric's day configuration has not yet been imported
acceptance_criteria.when: the user opens Calendaric's settings
then: a banner offers to import the folder, format and template from the core Daily Notes plugin

acceptance_criteria.given: the user accepts the import offer
acceptance_criteria.when: the import runs
then: Calendaric's day folder is set to the core Daily Notes plugin's folder
Calendaric's day format is set to the core Daily Notes plugin's format
Calendaric's day template is set to the core Daily Notes plugin's template
day is marked enabled
the import is recorded as completed

acceptance_criteria.given: the core Daily Notes plugin's stored format is empty
acceptance_criteria.when: the import runs
then: Calendaric's day format is set to a documented default date format instead of being left empty

acceptance_criteria.given: the import has already completed once
acceptance_criteria.when: the user opens Calendaric's settings again
then: the import banner does not reappear
running the import again leaves the day folder, format and template unchanged

acceptance_criteria.given: the user has already set a day folder, format or template in Calendaric before running the import
acceptance_criteria.when: the import would overwrite one of those values
then: Calendaric shows the incoming value next to the user's current value
the value is only replaced after the user confirms

acceptance_criteria.given: the core Daily Notes plugin is not enabled
acceptance_criteria.when: the user opens Calendaric's settings
then: no Daily Notes import banner is shown

stories.title: Disable the core Daily Notes plugin after import, with consent
stories.story: As someone who has just imported my Daily Notes configuration into Calendaric, I want to be asked before Calendaric turns the old plugin off, so that I keep control over a change to my setup that I did not directly ask for.
stories.rationale: Disabling another plugin is a destructive action on the user's configuration and must never happen as a silent side effect of import.

acceptance_criteria.given: the user has just imported the Daily Notes configuration
acceptance_criteria.when: Calendaric offers to disable the core Daily Notes plugin
then: the offer explains that the plugin will be turned off
the offer warns that hotkeys bound to the old plugin's commands may stop working
no plugin is disabled until the user responds

acceptance_criteria.given: the user confirms the offer to disable the plugin
acceptance_criteria.when: Calendaric disables it
then: the core Daily Notes plugin is turned off
Calendaric continues creating and opening day notes using the imported configuration

acceptance_criteria.given: the user declines or dismisses the offer
acceptance_criteria.when: the import finishes
then: the core Daily Notes plugin is left enabled and unmodified

acceptance_criteria.given: Calendaric has disabled the core Daily Notes plugin
acceptance_criteria.when: the user re-enables it from Obsidian's own plugin list afterwards
then: the plugin re-enables normally
no configuration or note data was deleted by Calendaric's earlier disable action

acceptance_criteria.given: the core Daily Notes plugin is already disabled or cannot be found when the disable action runs
acceptance_criteria.when: Calendaric attempts to disable it
then: Calendaric does not throw an error or crash

stories.title: Import weekly configuration and display preferences from the Calendar plugin
stories.story: As someone who uses the Calendar plugin today, I want Calendaric to offer to copy its weekly note settings and display preferences, so that switching plugins does not reset how my week view looks or behaves.
stories.rationale: No predecessor plugin ever imported Calendar-plugin settings into another plugin's configuration; this is new behaviour needed because Calendaric absorbs the Calendar plugin's role.

acceptance_criteria.given: the Calendar plugin is installed and its weekly note folder, format or template are set
acceptance_criteria.when: the user imports from the Calendar plugin
then: Calendaric's week folder, week format and week template are set from the same configuration the Calendar plugin actually uses to create weekly notes
week is marked enabled

acceptance_criteria.given: the Calendar plugin's settings screen also shows its own weekly folder/format/template fields, which the Calendar plugin no longer reads when creating notes
acceptance_criteria.when: Calendaric imports weekly configuration from the Calendar plugin
then: the imported values come from the configuration the Calendar plugin actually uses, not from its unused settings-screen fields

acceptance_criteria.given: the Calendar plugin's week-start day, confirm-before-create toggle, week-number display toggle and locale override are set
acceptance_criteria.when: the user imports from the Calendar plugin
then: Calendaric's week start, confirm-before-create, show-week-numbers and locale override settings are set to the matching Calendar plugin values

acceptance_criteria.given: the Calendar plugin also stores a words-per-dot setting
acceptance_criteria.when: the import runs
then: that value is not transferred, because this configuration has no equivalent field for it

acceptance_criteria.given: the user has already customised Calendaric's week folder, format or template
acceptance_criteria.when: the import would overwrite one of those values
then: Calendaric shows the incoming value next to the user's current value
the value is only replaced after the user confirms

acceptance_criteria.given: the Calendar plugin is not installed or not enabled
acceptance_criteria.when: the user looks for this import option
then: it is not offered

decisions.title: An import with nothing to import is not offered
decisions.decision: When a predecessor plugin's configuration is empty for every field the importer would read, that import is not offered at all.
decisions.rationale: In this vault the Calendar plugin's weekly fields are blank because weekly configuration lives in Periodic Notes. Offering to import nothing is noise that teaches users to dismiss the import prompt without reading it.

stories.title: Import per-granularity configuration from the Periodic Notes plugin's active calendar set
stories.story: As someone who configured day, week, month and year notes through the Periodic Notes plugin, I want Calendaric to import exactly what is actually in effect for each of those, so that my real settings survive the switch instead of a stale leftover value.
stories.rationale: This vault's Periodic Notes configuration currently disagrees with itself between an old top-level format and its live calendar set; getting this wrong would silently import the wrong folder and template.

acceptance_criteria.given: the Periodic Notes plugin's active calendar set enables a granularity with a folder, format and template
acceptance_criteria.when: the user imports from the Periodic Notes plugin
then: Calendaric's matching folder, format, template and enabled fields for that granularity are set from the active calendar set's values

acceptance_criteria.given: the Periodic Notes plugin's stored data still contains an older top-level key for a granularity alongside its active calendar set, and that top-level key names a different folder and template than the active calendar set's value for the same granularity
acceptance_criteria.when: the user imports from the Periodic Notes plugin
then: the imported folder and template match the active calendar set's values
the disagreeing top-level key's values are never applied to Calendaric's configuration

acceptance_criteria.given: the Periodic Notes plugin defines more than one calendar set
acceptance_criteria.when: the user imports from the Periodic Notes plugin
then: only the currently active calendar set is imported
the other calendar sets are neither imported nor merged into the active one

acceptance_criteria.given: the user has already customised one of Calendaric's per-granularity settings
acceptance_criteria.when: the import would overwrite it
then: Calendaric shows the incoming value next to the user's current value
the value is only replaced after the user confirms

acceptance_criteria.given: the import has already completed once and the Periodic Notes configuration has not changed since
acceptance_criteria.when: the user runs the import again
then: Calendaric's settings are left exactly as they were
no granularity is re-marked as needing review

acceptance_criteria.given: the Periodic Notes plugin is not installed or not enabled
acceptance_criteria.when: the user looks for this import option
then: it is not offered

decisions.title: Prefix matching is carried across on import
decisions.decision: The per-granularity allow-prefix-matching flag transfers from the Periodic Notes configuration into the imported configuration. It is not dropped.
decisions.rationale: The field has a direct equivalent in the new model. Dropping it silently turns off prefix matching for a vault that depends on it, and this vault does depend on it: its weekly notes are renamed to a longer title after creation and only resolve through a prefix match.

stories.title: Choose which predecessor plugin's configuration governs a granularity when more than one is active
stories.story: As someone who has both the core Daily Notes plugin and the Periodic Notes plugin configured for the same period, I want Calendaric to pick the same source it always used to, so that importing does not quietly switch me to a different set of settings than the ones actually taking effect today.
stories.rationale: Daily notes settings in the old plugins came from whichever of these plugins the code checked first; a merged importer must keep that precedence or it imports settings the vault was not actually using.

acceptance_criteria.given: the Periodic Notes plugin is installed and its active calendar set enables a granularity
acceptance_criteria.when: Calendaric resolves which predecessor configuration governs that granularity
then: the Periodic Notes plugin's configuration for that granularity is treated as authoritative, regardless of what the core Daily Notes plugin or the Calendar plugin are set to

acceptance_criteria.given: the Periodic Notes plugin is absent, or does not have day enabled in its active calendar set
acceptance_criteria.when: Calendaric resolves which predecessor configuration governs day notes
then: the core Daily Notes plugin's configuration is used if that plugin is enabled

acceptance_criteria.given: none of the predecessor plugins are enabled for a granularity
acceptance_criteria.when: Calendaric resolves which predecessor configuration governs that granularity
then: it reports the granularity as having no external configuration to import
it does not throw an error

acceptance_criteria.given: the Periodic Notes plugin instance is present but exposes no way to read which granularities are currently active in its installed version
acceptance_criteria.when: Calendaric checks whether it governs a granularity
then: Calendaric treats that granularity as not externally configured rather than guessing from a settings object that may not reflect the plugin's real state

acceptance_criteria.given: the same resolution is needed for day, week, month and year
acceptance_criteria.when: Calendaric performs this resolution
then: one shared resolution routine is used for all four granularities instead of a separate implementation per granularity

decisions.title: Probe exactly one canonical plugin id per predecessor
decisions.decision: Calendaric detects the core Daily Notes plugin, the Calendar plugin and the Periodic Notes plugin by one canonical id each, to offer a one-time import and to warn when a predecessor is still managing the same notes. The paired development-build id probe is not carried forward. Whether a predecessor owns a granularity is decided by its own enabled flag, checked the same way for every granularity.
decisions.rationale: The dual-id probe existed only to let a development build and a store build of the same plugin coexist in one vault. The merged plugin removes that situation. The old asymmetry, where the mere presence of the Calendar plugin counted as proof that weekly notes were externally managed, goes with it.

stories.title: Notice a predecessor plugin is still active and avoid double-managing periodic notes
stories.story: As someone who has not yet removed my old periodic-notes plugins, I want Calendaric to tell me when one of them is still switched on, so that I do not end up with two plugins both trying to create or manage the same notes without my knowledge.
stories.rationale: This vault currently has the core Daily Notes plugin, the Calendar plugin and the Periodic Notes plugin all enabled at once, so this coexistence risk exists from the moment Calendaric is installed, not only in edge cases.

acceptance_criteria.given: the core Daily Notes plugin, the Calendar plugin, or the Periodic Notes plugin is still enabled after the user has imported its configuration into Calendaric
acceptance_criteria.when: Calendaric starts
then: a visible notice tells the user that a predecessor plugin is still active for at least one granularity
Calendaric does not silently let both plugins create or manage notes for the same period

acceptance_criteria.given: none of the three predecessor plugins remain enabled
acceptance_criteria.when: Calendaric starts
then: no coexistence notice is shown

acceptance_criteria.given: a predecessor plugin is installed under exactly one canonical plugin id
acceptance_criteria.when: Calendaric checks whether that plugin is present
then: it probes that single id only

acceptance_criteria.given: Obsidian's plugin registry cannot be queried for some reason when this check runs
acceptance_criteria.when: Calendaric checks whether a predecessor plugin is enabled
then: it treats the plugin as not enabled rather than throwing an error

decisions.title: Probe exactly one canonical plugin id per predecessor
decisions.decision: Calendaric detects the core Daily Notes plugin, the Calendar plugin and the Periodic Notes plugin by one canonical id each, to offer a one-time import and to warn when a predecessor is still managing the same notes. The paired development-build id probe is not carried forward. Whether a predecessor owns a granularity is decided by its own enabled flag, checked the same way for every granularity.
decisions.rationale: The dual-id probe existed only to let a development build and a store build of the same plugin coexist in one vault. The merged plugin removes that situation. The old asymmetry, where the mere presence of the Calendar plugin counted as proof that weekly notes were externally managed, goes with it.

stories.title: Load Calendaric's own stored configuration safely across versions
stories.story: As someone who keeps this plugin updated, I want Calendaric to keep working with my existing settings after an update, so that a plugin upgrade never quietly resets or breaks my folders, formats and templates.
stories.rationale: Calendaric's stored configuration shape will change over time; none of the predecessor plugins actually implemented this (their own version field was written but never read back), so this has to be built new rather than ported.

acceptance_criteria.given: the stored configuration was written by an older version of Calendaric whose settings shape differs from the current one
acceptance_criteria.when: Calendaric loads it
then: the settings are upgraded to the current shape
no configured folder, format, template or toggle value already present in the old file is lost

acceptance_criteria.given: the stored configuration was written by a newer version of Calendaric than the one currently running
acceptance_criteria.when: Calendaric loads it
then: Calendaric starts successfully
any field it does not recognise is not treated as an error
it falls back to a safe default for anything it cannot interpret

acceptance_criteria.given: the stored configuration is not valid JSON, or has been hand-edited into an invalid shape such as a folder field holding a number instead of a string
acceptance_criteria.when: Calendaric loads it
then: it falls back to default settings for the invalid parts
it tells the user that some settings could not be read and were reset
the plugin does not crash

acceptance_criteria.given: the configuration has already been upgraded to the current shape once
acceptance_criteria.when: the vault is opened again with the same version
then: the upgrade routine does not run a second time
the stored file is not rewritten unnecessarily

acceptance_criteria.given: upgrading the stored configuration fails partway through
acceptance_criteria.when: Calendaric writes the result back to disk
then: either the fully upgraded settings are saved, or the original file is left completely untouched
a partially-written configuration file is never left on disk

decisions.title: Unrecognised configuration fields survive a round trip
decisions.decision: Configuration written by a newer version keeps its unrecognised fields when an older version loads and saves the file.
decisions.rationale: Same principle as preserving an unused named configuration group: running an older build once must not silently destroy settings, so that downgrading and upgrading again is safe.

notes: The real disagreement between periodic-notes-anks's stale top-level 'monthly' key and its live calendarSets[0].month value (folder '_00 Planer/_03a Miesiące Work' / template 'Monthly work.md' vs. the correct '_00 Planer/_03 Miesiące' / 'Monthly Periodic Template.md') is recorded in calendaric-map.json as an observation, not as a capability, so it has no uid to cite in constrained_by. AC-MIG-04.2 encodes it directly.

Three of the fifteen build capabilities in this slice (cal:daily-notes-plugin-warning-banner, pn:getting-started-banner-daily-notes-detection) are UI banners best exercised manually; most of the rest need a real Obsidian plugin instance to test meaningfully, so this epic leans integration/manual rather than unit.

No predecessor plugin ever imported the Calendar plugin's or the Periodic Notes plugin's configuration into another plugin's settings -- only the Daily Notes import path (calendaric:import-daily-notes-settings) existed before. US-MIG-03 and US-MIG-04's Periodic-Notes-facing half, and all of US-MIG-07, are therefore new behaviour with no old capability to point to in 'covers'.

Cross-plugin detection by plugin id is still needed for the three named predecessor plugins (core Daily Notes, Calendar, Periodic Notes) to drive imports and the coexistence notice in US-MIG-06 -- see that story's open_questions for why the old dev/production dual-id probe specifically should not carry forward.
